# three-slicer — kernel parameter reference

The FFF kernel's accepted parameter set, generated from the kernel's own reader (`params.cpp`) — see
[README.md](README.md) for install/usage and how these params are produced from an OrcaSlicer settings map.

Generated from the kernel's own reader (`params.cpp`) — it is the definition of the accepted key set, so this table
cannot drift from what `slice()` actually honours. Regenerate with `node types/gen_kernel_params.mjs`.

<!-- KERNEL-PARAMS:BEGIN — generated by types/gen_kernel_params.mjs, do not edit by hand -->

The kernel accepts **160 parameters**. `deriveKernelParams()` produces 131 of them from the
OrcaSlicer settings map; the remaining 29 have no schema key behind them and can only be set by writing
the params object directly — those rows show `—` in the *From setting* column.

A parameter left out of the object keeps the default listed here, so sending a partial object is normal and is
what `deriveKernelParams()` itself does.

*From setting* names the schema key the value is read from, which is often **not** the same name and not the
same unit — `first_layer_height` comes from `initial_layer_print_height`, and `infill_density` is
`sparse_infill_density` divided by 100 (a settings map holding `20` produces `0.2` here).

## The parameters no setting reaches

A `—` in *From setting* means there is no OrcaSlicer option behind that parameter, so it exists only if you put it
in the params object yourself. They are not one kind of thing, and the difference matters before you reach for one:

- **Host runtime flags** — `economy`, `keep_stages`, `reuse_stages`, `time_engine`, `wipe_tower_real`,
  `gcode_stats_block`, `gcode_config_block`, `gcode_role_tags`. Decisions the *caller* makes about a particular run, not properties of
  the print. `economy` is the last rung of an out-of-memory retry: it streams G-code and skips the preview
  toolpaths and the time estimate, so a model that cannot finish any other way still finishes.
- **Values the viewer computes** — `extruder_count`, `mm_group_split`, `mm_group_splits`, `mm_group_tools`,
  `auto_center`. These come from the scene (how many extruders are loaded, which triangle ranges belong to which
  tool), so there is nothing for a settings map to hold. `<Viewport/>` fills them in at slice time.
- **Kernel-only tuning** — `support_density`, `support_auto`, `support_grid_snap`, `support_overhang_min_area`,
  `tree_style`, `tree_lite_shrink`, `tree_lite_min_radius`, `scarf_length`, `prime_tower_ring_size`,
  `raft_first_layer_height`, `extrusion_rate_slope_segment_length`. Real knobs with no upstream option of the same
  name — some are this kernel's own approximations (the `tree_lite_*` taper), others are upstream behaviour that
  upstream never exposed as a setting.
- **Diagnostics** — `arachne_dump`, `pe_lite`, `pe_strip_tags`, `pe_external_perimeter_only`, `emit_pe_tags`. Left
  at their defaults unless you are working on the kernel itself. `pe_lite` in particular defaults to `true` because
  the real pressure equalizer only acts on G-code carrying OrcaSlicer's `;_EXTRUDE_SET_SPEED` tags, which this
  kernel emits only when asked.
